gloss: dramatic pose (in kabuki); striking a pose

definitions.gloss: dramatic pose (in kabuki); striking a pose
definitions.explanation: A stylized, frozen pose held by a kabuki actor at a climactic moment, often with crossed eyes and an exaggerated expression. By extension, any showy or boastful display of resolve.

examples.japanese: {役者|やくしゃ}が{見得|みえ}を{切|き}った。
examples.english: The actor struck a dramatic pose.

examples.japanese: {歌舞伎|かぶき}の{見得|みえ}は{観客|かんきゃく}が{一番|いちばん}{盛|も}り{上|あ}がる{瞬間|しゅんかん}だ。
examples.english: The mie pose is the moment in kabuki when the audience gets most excited.

examples.japanese: 「{絶対|ぜったい}{勝|か}ってみせる」と{大|おお}きな{見得|みえ}を{切|き}ったが、{結果|けっか}は{惨敗|ざんぱい}だった。
examples.english: He made a big show of declaring "I'll definitely win," but the result was a crushing defeat.

notes:
Almost always appears in the idiom {見得|みえ}を{切|き}る (to strike a dramatic pose). In the figurative sense, it describes making a bold declaration or showy display of resolve — often with an implication that the speaker may not deliver.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見得|みえ}を{切|き}る: to strike a pose; to make a bold declaration
- {大|おお}きな{見得|みえ}を{切|き}る: to make a grand show of resolve
- {見得|みえ}を{張|は}る: to put on airs (less common variant)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見栄|みえ}: vanity, showing off — same reading, related etymologically, but refers to outward appearance for social effect rather than a theatrical pose. {見栄|みえ}を{張|は}る = to keep up appearances
- ポーズ: pose — loanword, generic and modern
- {大言壮語|たいげんそうご}: big talk, grandiose words — emphasizes the boastful claim rather than the pose

prominent_see_also.note: vanity, showing off - same reading, different kanji
